test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 17 March, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

All bark and no bite

options.text: Someone who sticks to his words
Actions are stronger than mere words
Not being able to understand anything
Full of talk, but low on action

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"All bark and no bite" **refers to someone who talks tough or threatens others, but is actually not harmful or likely to take action.(धमकी देने वाला पर कार्रवाई नहीं करने वाला)
 
• The **most appropriate meaning** for this idiom is: **Full of talk, but low on action**

Therefore, the** correct answer** is: *'Full of talk, but low on action'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here are explanations for the rest of the options:
 
 
• **Someone who sticks to his words - **This suggests a person who follows through on their promises or threats, which is the opposite of "All bark and no bite".
 
• **Actions are stronger than mere words -** This phrase expresses the idea that actions have more impact than merely talking about something, which isn't the precise meaning of "All bark and no bite".
 
• **Not being able to understand anything -** This doesn't relate to the meaning of "All bark and no bite" at all. The idiom does not refer to confusion or a lack of understanding.
